context.body: Jesus distinguishes himself from the Father while making himself the decisive disclosure of the Father.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Jesus names himself as way, truth, and life, says knowing him means knowing the Father, and speaks of mutual indwelling through words and works.
observations.label: Seeing Jesus is tied to seeing the Father: action

observations.body: Philip asks to see the Father; Jesus directs attention to his own presence and works.
observations.label: Seeing Jesus is tied to seeing the Father: response

observations.body: through me · seen the Father · in the Father · words and works
observations.label: Words in John 14:6–11

payload.posture: Read John 14:6–11 as jesus and god evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: “Seen the Father” is relational and revelatory language; the passage does not say the Father and Son are the same person.
payload.title: Seeing Jesus is tied to seeing the Father
